Tesla is an oddball among the Mag 7

It's fundamentally a cyclical consumer/auto manufacturer that has been priced and grouped as a high‑margin, scalable software/AI platform.

It's the only member whose core revenue is selling physical vehicles and energy products in the Consumer sector.

It doesn't sell software, cloud, semiconductors, and digital advertising as a core business like the other Mag 7 names.

But unlike the other Mag 7 names, $TSLA is sitting on a huge goldmine of upside. 

There are three trends that Tesla is riding:

1) a gigantic EV transition
2) software-style monetization of vehicles
3) the rise in robotaxi services

The Mag 7 idea is about businesses that can compound earnings and cash flows at very high rates for a long time, not just current margins. 

Tesla is the only pure‑play global EV + autonomy platform at scale, with hundreds of billions in market cap already discounting a large share of future software and services value.

Tesla also owns the full stack: vehicle hardware, battery integration, in‑house software, over‑the‑air updates, and its own AI training stack, which is what underpins FSD and any future robotaxi network. 

That vertical integration makes Tesla much closer to the Mag 7 idea than to legacy auto.

Tesla's auto business, which is the main money maker of the business, is entering 2026 with pessimistic expectations.

What analysts (and even Tesla's own management team) don't realize is that labor markets have hit a cyclical bottom late Q3 of last year and have been exhibiting signs of a cyclical recovery ever since. 

Those many college grads struggling to find great work are going to get a job this year.

Those underemployed workers, fortunate to have a job but aren't at their fullest potential, are gonna get better jobs this year.

What do these folks have in common? They tend to be young and grew up aspiring to own a Tesla vehicle when they graduate and get a good job.

There's plenty of pent-up demand for Tesla vehicles that will turn into sales for the company this year.

Plus, since many jobs are in the office, with traffic being frustrating, many of these college grads and young workers are going to want to own a car that can drive them to work and home.

Tesla is the only automaker that produces cars that can do that. Rivian, Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, GMC, and all other automakers don't have driving assistance features that can match Tesla FSD.

When you understand this, you understand why $TSLA continued to fight resistance and trend higher despite the expiration of the EV tax credits at the end of Q3'25. 

On top of that, Tesla has expanded its sales presence into many emerging market nations, like:

- Philippines
- Chile
- India
- Saudi Arabia

And many more countries, all in 2025 alone. Many of these countries are resource-rich and benefit from the commodities boom and from these countries' inclination towards free markets.

The Middle Class is booming in all of these countries, and in all the other emerging market nations in which Tesla operates. 

So there is a huge swath of people living in these emerging market nations who will be able to afford Tesla vehicles this year.

We've seen Tesla sales soar in Korea this year. To the point where Korea became the 3rd largest sales market for Tesla at one point.

We will see similar spikes in sales in those countries as well throughout 2026.

The stock markets of those countries will soar because of the commodities boom. 

People will get rich from buying and holding stocks in their home country. 

And they'll use their riches to buy their dream car...a Tesla

For energy, robotaxis, Semi, Optimus, those things are self-explanatory.

More Tesla vehicles on the road means more FSD subscriptions which means more recurring revenue for Tesla. 

Enjoy the weekend! We are in good hands for 2026.
